citation: J.-M. Muller, "Elementary Functions: Algorithms and Implementation", 3rd ed., Birkhauser, 2016
title: Elementary Functions: Algorithms and Implementation

segments.title: Front Matter
segments.why: The chapter is front matter and contains no arithmetic-unit design detail.

segments.title: Introduction
segments.why: The chapter introduces elementary-function accuracy and implementation goals without describing a specific hardware mechanism.

segments.title: Some Basic Things About Computer Arithmetic
segments.why: The chapter defines floating-point formats/rounding and numerical properties rather than arithmetic-unit microarchitectures.

segments.title: Polynomial or Rational Approximations
segments.why: The chapter develops polynomial/rational approximation and evaluation methods that determine elementary-function polynomial datapaths.

segments.title: Table-Based Methods
segments.why: The chapter describes table lookup, domain segmentation, and table-plus-polynomial tradeoffs for elementary-function units.

segments.title: Multiple-Precision Evaluation of Functions
segments.why: The chapter concerns multiple-precision software packages and numerical algorithms rather than hardware arithmetic units.

segments.title: Introduction to Shift-and-Add Algorithms
segments.why: The chapter develops iterative shift-and-add mechanisms for computing exponential/logarithmic functions.

segments.title: The CORDIC Algorithm
segments.why: The chapter defines and evaluates CORDIC rotation/vectoring iterations and their hardware implementation properties.

segments.title: Some Other Shift-and-Add Algorithms
segments.why: The chapter describes high-radix shift-and-add recurrences that reduce elementary-function iteration counts.

segments.title: Range Reduction
segments.why: The chapter develops additive/multiplicative range-reduction mechanisms and their implementation accuracy requirements.

segments.title: Final Rounding
segments.why: The chapter analyzes implementation strategies for monotonic and correctly rounded elementary-function results.

segments.title: Miscellaneous
segments.why: The chapter discusses exceptional-case semantics without presenting an arithmetic-unit mechanism.

segments.title: Examples of Implementation
segments.why: The chapter examines processor implementations that combine polynomial/rational evaluation, segmentation, range reduction, FMA use, and rounding control.

segments.title: Bibliography and Index
segments.why: The chapter is bibliography/index back matter and contains no original design discussion.
